key_insight: Fixing dataset bias in binding‑affinity data leads to substantially better generalization — models become more reliable on new chemotypes and unseen targets when training data bias is identified and corrected.
problem_solved: Binding‑affinity models are often trained on biased datasets (scaffold, label, or target imbalances) that create spurious shortcuts and poor out‑of‑distribution performance; the paper shows how addressing those biases improves real-world prediction accuracy.
method: Analyze and quantify sources of bias in commonly used binding‑affinity datasets (e.g., scaffold/label/target imbalance and non‑representative splits).
Apply bias mitigation strategies such as stratified/rescaffolded train/test splits, reweighting or subsampling to balance signals, and data curation to reduce confounders.
Validate improvements using OOD and external test sets to demonstrate enhanced generalization rather than just in‑sample gains.
impact: For ML practitioners in drug discovery, correcting dataset bias yields more trustworthy affinity models, reducing false leads and improving transfer to new chemical space — a practical step toward safer, more effective AI assistance in screening and lead optimization.
